structured_output.world_model:
W2 (empirical), after E030. Tip is E027: 5.878 s, 0.7547 (20/24/28/32 px at 15/25/30/30%, 8.75 epochs, 219 steps, batch 2000). It clears 0.753 on seeds 0-2 by about 0.17 pp, but held-out seeds give about 0.7526, so the real margin is about zero.

Mechanisms:
1. Epoch dial: about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch for 0.0-0.15 pp. Cheapest lever, but the tip is at the accuracy floor (E020, E023, E027).
2. EMA (+0.97 pp, E005) and Muon (+0.66 pp, E006) are in the tip. Lookahead settings look tuned: a harder pull (E025) and a longer interval (E030, -0.5 pp) both hurt.
3. Time tracks pixels and FLOPs, sublinearly on small maps. Early low-res is nearly free (E026). Dropping or shrinking the 28 px phase costs 0.3-0.5 pp (E018, E024).
4. Compute cuts on the 32 px tail cost about 0.3 pp per 0.5 s (E028).
5. wd, label smoothing, Muon lr, LR floor and warm-up are flat within noise (E013, E014, E016, E022, E029). E016's 0.7607 was a lucky draw.
6. Noise: identical code is bit-identical. Any change to step count or RNG use reshuffles the 3-seed mean by about ±0.2 pp. The held-out mean sits about 0.2 pp below the seeds 0-2 mean. Time noise is about 0.5%.

Misses: I overpredicted time on trims; savings run 2-5% larger than modelled. Deltas under 0.3 pp are unreadable. E030 was a real accuracy miss.

Unsure: whether any time-neutral booster exists, and whether the tip needs more epochs to be safely feasible.

forecasts.reason: Dropping 10% of easy samples cuts steps about 9%, but the loss scatter adds overhead and the fewer steps cost accuracy like the epoch dial. Base is E023 at 6.2 s, so time ends near E027's.
Zeroing label smoothing for the last 15% of steps is time-neutral. The accuracy effect is likely within noise, with a small chance of a gain from sharper logits.
Swapping 15% of 24 px steps to 20 px saves about 2.5% of time. Accuracy probably drops about 0.2 pp, which is borderline against the 0.752 keep bar.
Per-resolution whitening costs some extra prepare time and requires extra buffers. The accuracy effect is likely flat, because BN adapts to the stem statistics.

cruxes: Is the held-out 10-seed mean of the tip really below 0.753, so that any further time cut needs an accuracy booster first?
Is any time-neutral accuracy booster real (above 0.15 pp), or is everything within the +-0.2 pp reshuffle noise?
How much accuracy does extending the 20 px phase cost (I050), since it is the cheapest remaining time lever?
